title: Ukrainian Drones Ignite Fires at Saratov Oil Refinery and Ozon Warehouse in Russia
detail: Ukrainian long-range FP-1 drones, made by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point, struck Russia's Saratov Oil Refinery, owned by Rosneft, and a nearby 100,000-square-meter Ozon logistics warehouse overnight on September 10-11. Fires broke out at both sites; independent Russian outlet ASTRA's OSINT analysis identified a fire at the refinery, while Fire Point said the strike destroyed roughly 85,000 square meters of the Ozon depot and over 30 million stored items. Saratov Oblast Governor Roman Busargin posted an alert about the drone threat. No casualties were reported. President Zelensky said the strikes delivered 'good results from our long-range strikes aimed at reducing Russia's capacity to wage war.' The refinery has been repeatedly targeted during Ukraine's long-range campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.

title: Prosecutors Say Russian Forces Executed 2 Captured Ukrainian National Guard Soldiers Near Dobropillia
detail: The Donetsk Oblast Prosecutor's Office said on September 11 that Russian troops executed two captured Ukrainian National Guard servicemen near Dobropillia, Donetsk Oblast. According to the investigation, the two soldiers were at a firing position in a forest belt near Dobropillia on September 2 when they were captured by Russian forces and shot with automatic weapons shortly afterward. Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) is investigating the killings as a war crime under Article 438 of Ukraine's Criminal Code. The killing of prisoners of war is a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions; Ukrainian and international monitors have documented a pattern of similar summary executions of Ukrainian POWs by Russian forces since 2022.
